"Game Overview
A 2D side-scrolling, physics-based rocket-building and destruction game. Players construct custom missiles on a launch pad at their Home Base on the far left of a tall, expansive map and launch them across the terrain to demolish distant, multi-story enemy strongholds.
Core Gameplay Loop
 * Build: Assemble a custom rocket on an expanding grid next to Home Base using cheap, modular parts—rotating and positioning each piece to fine-tune balance, thrust, and aerodynamics.
 * Launch @COMMENT_BODY@ Steer: Control individual engines (each with its own 0%–100% thrust control), ignite stages, and steer mid-flight using aerodynamic fins, individual stage separators, and remote-detonated payloads.
 * Destroy @COMMENT_BODY@ Earn: Smash into enemy structures with full collision physics. Earn coins from defeated enemies, destroyed building parts, and bonus money boxes.
 * Upgrade @COMMENT_BODY@ Repeat: Spend coins in the upgrade menu to improve existing parts or unlock larger, specialized components. Buildings remain damaged between launches, resetting only when all enemies are eliminated or when manually triggered in the settings.
Rocket Building @COMMENT_BODY@ Components
Rockets are built on an expanding grid at the launch pad, where parts can be rotated in the build menu to create custom silhouettes, angled thrusters, or unconventional designs. Individual parts are inexpensive to encourage experimentation, while unlocking new component tiers and sizes requires a larger coin investment. Every component—not just warheads—deals kinetic damage upon impact.
 * Engines: Generate thrust, with each engine getting its own individual control in the UI (including a 0%–100% thrust slider) for independent firing and throttle management. Available in multiple sizes.
 * Fuel Tanks: Dictate how long the engines can burn. Available in multiple sizes.
 * Fins (Left @COMMENT_BODY@ Right): Allow mid-air steering. Placement matters: fins at the bottom push the tail of the rocket, while fins at the top push the nose.
 * Warheads: Deliver explosive payloads with varying blast yields based on size and upgrades.
 * Nose Cones: Improve aerodynamics and impact survivability. Includes Armor-Penetrating Nose Cones with significantly higher durability for punching through multiple floors.
 * Explosive Tanks: Same footprint as standard fuel tanks, equipped with a dedicated Detonate button in the UI for mid-air or delayed blasts.
 * Separators: Split the rocket into multiple stages mid-flight, with each separator getting its own individual button in the UI so players can detach specific sections on demand.
Level Design @COMMENT_BODY@ Destruction Physics
 * Enemy Clusters: Levels feature clusters of 5–10 buildings, each 2–6 floors tall, built with full collision physics.
 * Interactive Props: Buildings contain explosive barrels for chain-reaction damage and money boxes that award bonus coins.
 * Persistent Damage: Players can launch as many rockets as needed. Structures stay damaged across attempts and only reset once every enemy in the level is destroyed (or via the settings menu).
Camera, Map @COMMENT_BODY@ UI
 * Tall Map: Designed with high verticality so players rarely hit out-of-bounds limits.
 * Dynamic Camera: Automatically zooms out the higher the rocket flies to keep the trajectory and terrain readable.
 * Free Cam: A toggleable Free Cam button lets players pan and zoom freely across the map to scout enemy weak points.
 * Mini-Map (Corner HUD):
   * Green Line: Terrain profile
   * Blue Square: Home Base
   * Red Dots: Enemies
   * Blue Dot: Active rocket
   * Blue Parabolic Line: Live projected trajectory to the terrain
 * Settings Menu: Includes a Reset Level button and a +100 Coins button for testing or sandbox play. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

function renderFlightActions(){let group=$('#flightActions');group.innerHTML='';let separators=parts.filter(p=>p.type==='separator'&&p.attached!==false);separators.forEach((p,i)=>{let b=document.createElement('button');b.className='actionBtn secondary';b.textContent=`SPLIT ${i+1}`;b.onclick=()=>{let stageY=p.y;parts.forEach(q=>{if(q.y>stageY)q.attached=false});p.attached=false;showToast(`Stage ${i+1} separated.`);renderFlightControls();renderFlightActions()};group.appendChild(b)});let explosives=parts.filter(p=>p.type==='explosive'&&p.attached!==false);explosives.forEach((p,i)=>{let b=document.createElement('button');b.className='actionBtn warn';b.textContent=`✦ BLAST ${i+1}`;b.onclick=()=>{if(rocket){explode(rocket.x,rocket.y,130,7);p.attached=false;showToast('Explosive tank remotely detonated.');renderFlightActions()}};group.appendChild(b)});let b=document.createElement('button');b.className='actionBtn warn';b.id='detonateBtn';b.textContent='✹ WARHEAD';b.onclick=detonate;group.appendChild(b);if(phase==='result'){group.innerHTML='';let rb=document.createElement('button');rb.className='actionBtn secondary';rb.textContent='↺ REBUILD';rb.onclick=launchNext;group.appendChild(rb);if(structures.every(s=>!s.alive)){let nb=document.createElement('button');nb.className='actionBtn';nb.textContent='NEXT SECTOR →';nb.onclick=launchNext;group.appendChild(nb)}}}

Built **SKYBREAKER — Rocket Lab** as a playable, responsive browser game in `index.html`.

It includes a modular rocket builder, individual engine throttles, staging and remote detonation, persistent structure damage, coins and upgrades, a tactical minimap, free camera, and settings for resetting the level or adding coins.
